parsed.explanation: The passage inserts c into the König's-lemma branch and argues that at the next F_k containing c, the element selected there is dispensable. But the modified path is not shown to be a path of the constructed tree: after a node containing c, the tree's rule selects a set F_D disjoint from that node, so F_{k2} (which contains c) would not be selected there, and subsequent branchings/pruning decisions differ from the original branch. Nor is 'dispensable' defined so that deleting x_{k2+1} provably preserves transversality against all members of F (only F_{k2} is shown met by c). Hence the argument never establishes that the original, or indeed any, branch of the pruned tree contains a contracted node, so the contradiction with the pruning rule is a non-sequitur. The finite-blocker fact is true, but the write-up's proof of it fails as written, and the entire finiteness step (obligation F), on which the periodicity assembly rests, depends on this lemma.
